nodes.label: Client-Side Localized Starter Packs Flow
nodes.rationale: Moving the starter catalogue to the Flutter client so titles resolve through AppLocalizations fixes hard-coded English database rows that gen-l10n could never reach; POST /api/families accepts an optional starterTasks array, with absent meaning legacy English seeding and an empty array explicitly meaning start empty.

nodes.label: flutter gen-l10n Localization Approach
nodes.rationale: Each language lives in one ARB file; the SDK generator produces typed Dart getters so a string missing from any language file fails the build instead of silently falling back to English, and ICU syntax handles plurals/placeholders with no third-party dependency.

nodes.label: untranslated.json CI Guardrail
nodes.rationale: untranslated.json is regenerated on every build and must be empty before a release; a PR rule requires any change to app_en.arb to touch the other three ARB files in the same PR.

nodes.label: MyCareCoins Pro Entitlement
nodes.rationale: The identifier string 'MyCareCoins Pro' (including the space) is load-bearing in both PurchaseService.entitlementId (Flutter) and billingService.js's entitlement→plan mapping; a typo makes every entitlement check quietly return false.

nodes.label: Provider Swappability (RevenueCat Boundary)
nodes.rationale: Only the Flutter purchase trigger and the webhook consumer are RevenueCat-aware; family_plans/billing_events/entitlements/admin area are provider-neutral via a 'provider' column, so a future Stripe web checkout becomes a third writer into the same tables.

nodes.label: family_id Subscriber Attribute (Purchase Attribution)
nodes.rationale: Setting a family_id subscriber attribute just before the paywall replaced the planned purchase-intent-UUID endpoint, achieving the same store-purchase-to-family attribution with one moving part instead of three.

nodes.label: Production Deployment Probe
nodes.rationale: An unmounted route falls through to a 404 handler while a mounted one answers 401, so probing /api/personal-time, /api/admin/families and /api/billing/webhook tells you what backend version is actually deployed without needing credentials.

nodes.label: No E2E Layer on main (Gap)
nodes.rationale: The Playwright harness described in the doc is kept as a design model for a future Flutter integration_test/flutter drive equivalent, not as a suite anyone runs; money-moving paths are instead hand-verified against a throwaway Postgres 16 container.

nodes.label: Deliberate Test Pyramid
nodes.rationale: Risk-based unit testing on money-moving/consensus paths plus offline E2E against the Firebase emulator, including a two-browser cross-user validation test; known gaps are the auto-complete sweep, coverage measurement, and push delivery.

nodes.label: Family Heartbeat Mechanism
nodes.rationale: families.last_active_at is touched only on successful (<400) family-scoped responses, throttled to one write per family per hour, so an unauthorized probe cannot keep a family looking alive; buckets active/dormant/inactive drive the admin registry without touching content tables.

nodes.label: Admin Privacy Boundary (Landlord not Housemate)
nodes.rationale: users.platform_role is a global axis deliberately separate from family_members roles, so being an admin grants no rights inside any family; adminService maps every row through an explicit field allowlist and a CI leak-prevention test asserts only registry aggregates surface.

nodes.label: Inactivity Notice → Retention Sweep Process
nodes.rationale: Cleanup of dormant families is a process, not a button: admin sends an audited inactivity notice, then scripts/retention-sweep.js deletes only families that stayed silent past a waiting period, dry-run by default, re-verifying inactivity before the DELETE.

nodes.label: Parameterized Query Defense
nodes.rationale: Every client.query() call passes user values as $N params, never string-concatenated; the one dynamic SQL fragment (prefClause in notify.js) is guarded by a hardcoded whitelist Set, closing the only apparent injection surface.

nodes.label: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE Locking Pattern
nodes.rationale: Row-level lock taken inside a single transaction (validate, complete, offerBounty, runAutoCompleteSweep) so a concurrent second request blocks, then re-evaluates the committed status and is rejected cleanly, making double-minting of coins impossible without load-tested infrastructure.

nodes.label: Middleware / Routes / Services Layering
nodes.rationale: Middleware answers 'may this proceed', routes translate HTTP to domain calls with no logic of their own, services hold pure business rules against a transaction client with no HTTP knowledge — this boundary is what makes 44+ backend unit tests possible with a mock DB client.

nodes.label: Lazy Sweep-on-Read Pattern
nodes.rationale: Auto-completion runs lazily inside the same transaction as the read that follows, instead of a cron job, so it needs no scheduler, stays transactionally consistent with what the user is about to see, costs nothing for inactive families, and is concurrency-safe via FOR UPDATE row locks; trade-off is payouts wait until someone opens the app.

nodes.label: Firebase Auth Verification Chain
nodes.rationale: Firebase answers who the user is (stateless local JWT verification against cached Google public keys); the backend's own family_members RBAC answers what they may do, decoupled from Firebase UID via upsertUserFromAuth.

nodes.label: migrate-activity-subclasses.sql
nodes.rationale: The one migration among the six pending ones that rewrites existing activity rows rather than only adding to them: renames category→type and adds a new category. Rehearsed on 2026-08-28 against a Postgres 16 copy seeded with representative data with no data loss.

nodes.label: Activities as Base Class with Two Subclasses
nodes.norm_label: activities as base class with two subclasses
nodes.rationale: category (care/self) plus type (sub-type within it) turn a single activities table into a base class with two subclasses instead of two separate tables; self activities are always worth zero coins and excluded from every contribution figure.

nodes.label: Personal Time & Coverage Feature
nodes.rationale: A fairness tool that only measures what a caretaker gives is incomplete; personal time lets a caretaker book time for themselves that generates a matching zero-coin self activity and a paid coverage shift for the other caretaker. Declines are deliberately never counted anywhere so refusal stays free and the sweetener never becomes social pressure.

nodes.label: Entitlement Merge — Most Generous Wins
nodes.rationale: Effective entitlement merges the default plan, a subscription in good standing, and unrevoked admin grants; store truth and admin truth never overwrite each other, and only past_due status triggers the 402 read-only gate — other lapsed statuses downgrade gracefully.

nodes.label: generate-firebase-sw Vite Plugin
nodes.rationale: A service worker must be served as a static file at a fixed URL so it cannot go through Vite's bundler and read import.meta.env; a custom buildStart hook writes public/firebase-messaging-sw.js with config baked in from the same env vars the app uses, avoiding config drift or a runtime fetch race on a cold-woken worker.

nodes.label: Two Service Worker Architecture
nodes.rationale: Workbox SW (offline caching, autoUpdate) and firebase-messaging-sw.js (background push, own scope) coexist without conflict because Firebase registers its worker at a distinct push scope.

nodes.label: The Family Operations Room (Creative North Star)
nodes.norm_label: the family operations room (creative north star)
nodes.rationale: CareCoins is styled as the shared dashboard a family runs on: structured enough to carry real information, warm enough to feel like home, with warmth earned through legibility and fair representation rather than decorative softness.

nodes.label: Flat-by-Default, Ambient-on-State Elevation
nodes.rationale: Surfaces stack through background color, not shadows; a shadow appears only when an element needs to communicate lift (FAB, modal, hover) — a static non-interactive element should never carry one.

nodes.label: The One Job Rule (Semantic Color)
nodes.rationale: Every color has exactly one semantic role and stays in it — blue for action, green for done, amber for household, red for danger — so a new color usually means a state variation of an existing token, not a new hue.

nodes.label: Anti-Gamification / Anti-Feed Design Principle
nodes.rationale: Explicit anti-references to Facebook/Instagram engagement-bait UI, cold corporate SaaS, and gamification-first design; coins are a fairness tool, and the app should feel finite and completable rather than an infinite feed.

nodes.label: scripts/deploy.sh
nodes.rationale: Refuses to run unless the tree is clean and pushed, backs up database and uploads before touching anything, then fast-forwards the server, rebuilds, probes the public API and prints the exact rollback command.

nodes.label: --reset-db Flag
nodes.rationale: Deliberately awkward because it destroys every family, activity and coin balance: forces a backup and refuses with --skip-backup, requires typing the host name (not bypassed by --yes), and verifies the result (families=0, personal_time_requests exists) rather than trusting the exit code.
